body:
FOLLOW-UP, decisive and short — the reviewer is the gate on this RIGHT NOW (phase 3, PR-2043).

TWO SUBSYSTEMS DISAGREE ABOUT WHO OWNS PR-2043, at this moment:

    aida drain status   ->  STORY-1391, in-phase-3, PR-2043
    events.jsonl        ->  01:52:45  BUG-1420  UnshippedWorkDetected  branch=pr-2043

The drain is driving it as STORY-1391's work. The unshipped-work detector reads the commit trailers and attributes the same PR to BUG-1420. Both are reading the same branch; only one can be right, and the trailers are the durable record.

AND THE SPEC STATES SHOW THE DAMAGE HAS ALREADY STARTED:

    STORY-1391   done          <- marked done on work that is not its own
    BUG-1420     in-progress   <- still open, while its commits sit on a PR
                                  the drain will merge under another spec

STORY-1391 was flipped to `done` at the end of an implementer phase that produced no STORY-1391 commit. That is not a future risk; it is on disk now. Merging PR-2043 would compound it by auto-bumping STORY-1391 to Completed and leaving BUG-1420 open with its work merged under someone else's id.

THE ASK IS UNCHANGED AND NOW MORE URGENT: hold #2043. The correct PR for that commit is #2042, whose branch name (`bug-1420-round2`) and trailers agree with each other.

I am not proposing a remedy for STORY-1391's status. Resetting a `done` spec that never had work is disposition, it is the advisor's, and I have been wrong twice today about what should be superseded or reset. What I am confident of is the factual claim: the two branches are byte-identical, neither carries STORY-1391 work, and the two subsystems disagree about the owner.
